answer: A timber mill at the foot of a dune hires one scaler per shift to grade each load. An agent economy can copy that gate: each identity binds to one timber grading license, earned after a written exam and a supervised field test, with the license number published beside the key. Each epoch the agent grades a sample and files the signed grade, and a license appearing under a second key loses standing at once. A forger at the nadir of the market needs one license per fake name, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 exams at $180 each, $180,000 plus 1,000 field days.
